summary: Tightened repository/no-comments so a permitted label must carry what makes it checkable: a suppression directive gives its reason, an accepted decision mention cites an ID, ruling date or question number, and a Platform: comment names its platform or tool. ESLint now also checks comments in config/*.d.mts files and **/*.ts.txt fixtures.
action: After the upgrade, bun run lint refuses three kinds of comment it used to admit. A suppression with no reason: add it after the directive (eslint-disable-next-line rule -- reason, fallow-ignore-next-line kind -- reason, @ts-expect-error reason, biome-ignore lint/group/rule: reason), or fix what it suppresses. An accepted decision mention with no citation: cite it right after the words (accepted decision N4a, or Accepted decision (Nathan, 19 November 2026, 12:08 AEDT), or Accepted decision (Command Contract 3 question 4)), or say it in code and delete the comment. A Platform: comment that names no platform or tool: name the one the fact is about (Bun, git, macOS, Linux, POSIX, TypeScript, a JavaScript built-in such as Map), or, when it describes the repository's own code, say it in a name or a test title and delete the comment. A run over current main found 0 such comments in wiki-personal's tool code and 3 in agent-cli-kernel (tests/kernel/approval/harness.ts:96 and tests/kernel/locks/lock-probes.test.ts:171 name no platform; tests/kernel/kernel-followup/fixtures/kf-cli.ts.txt:666 cites no decision, and bites only once the kernel lints .ts.txt fixtures).
